original_title: Ubisoft says the Black Flag remake has exceeded 'annual expectations' in just two weeks, shortly after it laid off a number of the people who made it

en.title: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Remake Shatters Sales Goals Amidst Layoff Controversy
en.summary: Ubisoft's remake of the beloved pirate adventure, Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, has achieved staggering success, exceeding annual sales expectations within its first two weeks. This financial triumph arrives as a stark reminder of recent workforce reductions within the company.
en.body:
The call of the high seas has never been stronger for Assassin's Creed fans. **Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced**, the freshly released remake of the 2013 fan-favorite, has made an immediate and significant impact on the market. In just its first day, the game sold an astonishing 2 million copies, a feat that set the stage for even greater financial success. Ubisoft CEO **Yves Guillemot** recently revealed that within two weeks of its launch, the title had already surpassed the company's entire annual sales projections.

"Two weeks in, the title has already exceeded the annual expectations we had," Guillemot stated in a financial report. "The strong launch of **Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced** in early July by Vantage Studios is an encouraging proof point. The game is the highest-rated Assassin's Creed title since the original Black Flag, and we are very pleased with the praise it received from players… I would like to warmly thank the teams whose talent and dedication brought it to life."

## A Conflicted Launch

However, Guillemot's commendations are overshadowed by a somber reality. The praise for **Black Flag Resynced** comes shortly after Ubisoft implemented significant layoffs, impacting hundreds of employees across various studios. Notably, nearly a third of **Ubisoft Barcelona**, a studio that contributed to the remake's development, specifically handling the underwater gameplay sections, was affected by these cuts, even leading to a labor strike. This juxtaposition of commercial success and workforce reduction has created a difficult narrative around the game's launch, highlighting the ongoing challenges within the gaming industry.

## Fan Reception and Future Prospects

Despite the behind-the-scenes turmoil, the remake's commercial performance suggests that the original **Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag** holds a special place in the hearts of many gamers. Its unique blend of naval combat, exploration, and a compelling pirate narrative has clearly endured. While some critics, like PC Gamer's **Morgan Park**, noted that the remake, despite being well-made, felt somewhat inessential and introduced changes like simplified combat and an in-game shop that didn't fully land, the sheer volume of players drawn to the experience is undeniable. The game's strong sales indicate that the core appeal of Edward Kenway's adventures remains potent enough to carry the remake forward, even with potential drawbacks.

## What's Next

With **Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced** exceeding all initial sales forecasts, Ubisoft is likely to see this as a strong indicator of the franchise's continued market viability. Further details regarding post-launch content or potential expansions have not yet been announced, but the game's impressive debut suggests a bright future for this particular entry in the long-running series.

content_raw: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, a game with a title that feels like it ought to have a colon or an em dash somewhere in there, is finally here and it's selling like whatever the nautical equivalent of hotcakes is. Hardtack, I guess. Not only did it sell 2 million copies in a single day , a recent financial report includes Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot saying "Two weeks in, the title has already exceeded the annual expectations we had." "The strong launch of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced in early July by Vantage Studios is an encouraging proof point," he said. "The game is the highest-rated Assassin's Creed title since the original Black Flag, and we are very pleased with the praise it received from players … I would like to warmly thank the teams whose talent and dedication brought it to life." Guillemot's thanks come at an interesting time, given that nearly a third of Ubisoft Barcelona was laid off just weeks ago, triggering a labor strike . This was part of a larger wave of layoffs which affected hundreds of workers. As it has done with a variety of Ubisoft games, Ubisoft Barcelona supported the development of Black Flag Resynced and "did all the underwater levels" as tech and gameplay animator Manel Cota posted on X back then. Regardless, the ludicrous sales Black Flag Resynced is enjoying seem like a signal that the original game's reputation is strong enough to carry this remake through potential turnoffs for prospective players, such as the day one DLC , simplified swordfights , and in-game shop . In his review, PC Gamer's Morgan Park called the game "a well-made, but inessential remake that loses more than it gains."
